records.title: A Procedure for Selection of Diving and Aviation Personnel Resistant to Decompression Sickness Based on Tests in a Low Pressure Chamber
records.authors: W. Welham, J. J. Blanch, A. R. Behnke
records.ages_in_table_note: The printed records include older ages, including age 34 in Table I. Preserve the printed values.
records.cardiovascular_score_note: The authors define a step-up score from two post-exercise pulse measurement windows. They report administering the test at the beginning and end of training and give one score per participant in the table.
records.specific_gravity_note: Preserved as printed, without rescaling. Four Table I cells are blank.
records.retests_note: Repeat flights after intestinal-gas pain were described. Counts and participant linkage for those attempts are unavailable.
records.test_1_time_note: Table III explicitly labels time at altitude before bends. Tables I and II report duration of stay.
records.qualification_note: All men were described as qualified for Navy service and deep-sea diving. Fair and good groups were assigned after Test 1.
records.note: The Methods mention 110 exposed men. The Results categorize 100 for Test 1. The report does not account for the ten-person difference or give counts of repeated attempts after intestinal-gas pain.

observations.protocol: Naval chamber at room temperature, 38,000 ft simulated altitude, ascent 5,000 ft/min. The report describes oxygen during ascent and at altitude and gives no measured fraction or surface lead time. The first hour was at rest. Intermittent exercise was scheduled in the second hour.
observations.outcome_window: Up to 120 minutes at 38,000 ft. Systematic observation beyond the chamber test was not reported.
observations.note: Sum of the 22 first-hour and 40 second-hour failures among 100 classified men. Only 78 participant rows are printed across the three tables.

observations.outcome_window: First hour after attaining 38,000 ft in Test 1. The denominator is the full classified Test 1 group.
observations.note: Source-labeled poor group. Table III has 21 individual times before bends. These 22 failures are included in the 62-failure margin.

observations.protocol: Naval chamber at room temperature, 38,000 ft simulated altitude, ascent 5,000 ft/min. The report describes oxygen during ascent and at altitude and gives no measured fraction or surface lead time. Exercise began 10 minutes after arrival at altitude and repeated every 10 minutes. Tests selected men from the fair and good Test 1 groups.
observations.outcome_window: Up to 120 minutes at 38,000 ft. Systematic observation beyond the chamber test was not reported.
observations.note: Results indicate 26 failures. Table II shows 26 durations shorter than 120 min. The counts cannot be added to Test 1 as independent people.
